text:
Treaties are to be interpreted in good faith, in accordance with the ordinary meaning of their terms in context and in light of the treaty's object and purpose (Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties 1969, Art. 31(1)). The "object and purpose" is only one element of that rule, not the sole test, so the second option (object and purpose alone) is wrong. Supplementary means such as the travaux préparatoires may be used only to confirm that meaning or when it remains ambiguous or absurd (Art. 32).

CONFIDENCE: 97
